_comment: Golden vectors for AP2's receipts — the verifier's signed answer to a
closed mandate, mandatory on rejection as well as on success.
No token is pinned here, and the reason is the same one golden_test.go
gives for not pinning a whole signed mandate: a receipt is a compact JWS
signed with ECDSA, which draws a fresh nonce for every signature, so two
runs over identical input produce different bytes.
The reference cannot be pinned either, and that is worth stating because
it is not obvious. reference is sd_hash, which is a digest over the
issuer-signed JWT together with the disclosures present — and that JWT
carries the mandate's own ECDSA signature. So the reference of a given
mandate is stable for one presentation and unreproducible across
issuances, even with the salts pinned. What a second implementation has
to reproduce is the rule, which the suite asserts directly: the reference
equals the sd_hash of the presentation the verifier was shown, and
nothing the mandate itself claims.
What is pinned is what two implementations have to agree on by name.
AP2 fixes only 'reference'; the rest is this project's encoding, recorded
in docs/specs/2026-08-06-receipts-design.md. Registered JWT claims are
used where one already means the thing — iss for the answering party and
iat for when it answered — so a generic JWT reader sees a coherent token
rather than a bag of custom names.
typ is not decoration. Mandates and receipts are both compact JWS signed
by the same keys, so a verifier that reads the claims it expected and
ignores the rest would accept whichever artefact it was handed.
